subject: Proposal: multi-year escrow tranche schedule + Net90 request
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@cloudfin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cloudfin.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudfin.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal and billing cadence

Ben — thanks for the proposal. Priya and I reviewed the MAP and list pricing; the technical fit looks great. Before we proceed to legal, finance has two asks we need to resolve: 1) CloudFin works on Net90 payment terms for multi-year vendors and would like the contract to reflect Net90 on invoiced amounts after an initial prepay; 2) because of our internal audit windows, we prefer a tranche/milestone billing schedule (30% upfront, 40% at year 1 completion, 30% at year 2) rather than a single annual prepay.

Can Redwood accommodate Net90 for the tail payments if we provide an upfront partial prepay (30%)? Also include any compliance/escrow options we can show procurement.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is targeting an Aug 12 signature.

—Liam
Head of Cloud Procurement
CloudFin

Attachments: CloudFin-finance-requested-milestone-schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@cloudfin.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal and billing cadence

Liam — thanks for the clear asks and the milestone schedule. High level response: we can be flexible on billing cadence, but Net90 on outstanding invoices is an exception for our standard prepay model and needs approval. Two options for quick alignment:

1) Partial prepay + milestone invoicing: 30% upfront prepay (applied to year 1 consumption), 50% invoiced as milestone at year 1 completion with Net30, remaining 20% invoiced at year 2 completion with Net90 (or 30/40/30 per your spreadsheet if you prefer) — pricing would need to reflect the extended credit exposure.

2) Escrow/letters of credit: If CloudFin is willing to place the billed-but-not-paid portion under an escrow arrangement or provide a standby LOC, we can extend Net90 on those amounts while keeping higher prepay coverage and preserving our unit economics.

I'm looping in Ava (SE) to confirm that the consumption profile and model pins match the milestone cadence, and Evelyn from legal to scope contract language and security requirements for escrow/LOC terms.

Can you confirm which tranche split CloudFin prefers and whether procurement can consider an LOC? If neither is feasible, we can propose a blended discount that bridges the cost of credit.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call this week.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 2026-08-01-CloudFin-MAP-and-pricing-proposal.pdf (proposal stub)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@cloudfin.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cloudfin.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal and billing cadence

Liam/Ben — quick technical note: CloudFin's projected ramp (see tab "expected_tokens") aligns with the 30/40/30 split in their spreadsheet. Operationally we'll need to pin model versions for year 1 so that cost-per-token projections hold; otherwise variance could create reconciliation headaches at milestone billing. Happy to add a simple clause that ties invoiced consumption to a pre-agreed prompt set for the milestone evaluation.

If Finance needs an SSO/traceability artifact for the escrow account, we can provide the audit log export and per-token usage breakdown at each milestone.

—Ava
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cloudfin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@cloudfin.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudfin.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal and billing cadence

Thanks — quick answers from finance: CloudFin cannot commit capital to an LOC right now. Their preference is: 30% upfront prepay, 40% invoiced after 12 months with Net90, 30% at contract end with Net90. They are open to a small fee/discount adjustment if Redwood requires it to cover credit exposure. Procurement is asking for a clause that limits Redwood's exposure to a maximum outstanding balance equal to one upcoming milestone.

We also need standard SOC2 evidence and confirmation that usage-based overages can be invoiced under the same Net90 terms.

Would Redwood consider 1.5% fee on the outstanding balance in exchange for Net90, or alternatively a 3% reduction to the committed discount?

Best,
Priya
Director, Vendor Finance
CloudFin

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal and billing cadence — legal touchpoint

Team — summarizing the ask from CloudFin and our constraints: they want Net90 on two milestone invoices (months 12 and contract end) with only 30% upfront. They also asked that outstanding exposure be capped at one upcoming milestone. From a legal/credit perspective we can accept Net90 on milestone invoices if one of the following is true: (A) CloudFin posts a limited escrow equal to one milestone; (B) CloudFin signs a vendor payment covenant (we can add events of default tied to nonpayment); or (C) they accept a modest fee (1–2%) to offset credit risk.

If leadership approves a fee-based path, finance should adjust the per-unit economics in the SOW and we must add: invoice aging remedies, recovery costs, and an explicit cap on outstanding liability. If leadership prefers to avoid fees, request an escrow or payment instrument.

Marissa — need decision on whether to permit the fee (1.5%) in exchange for Net90, or require escrow/LOC. CloudFin is timeboxed to Aug 12 for signature, so we should respond by EOD Aug 5.

—Evelyn
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal and billing cadence — decision

Team — after weighing relationship value and the strategic footprint CloudFin provides (large reference account in mid-market finance vertical), approve the fee-based path. Offer the following counter-proposal to CloudFin:

- Keep their preferred tranche: 30% upfront prepay; 40% invoiced at month 12; 30% at contract end.
- Redwood will accept Net90 on the two milestone invoices on the condition that CloudFin pays a 1.5% credit fee on the outstanding milestone amounts (applies only to amounts outstanding past 30 days).
- Redwood will cap our exposure to one milestone by reducing year-2 prepay eligibility if invoices age beyond 120 days.
- Include required SOC2 evidence and the usage reconciliation clause Ava suggested.

Ben — please send the revised SOW and pricing schedule reflecting the 1.5% fee and the exposure cap; include the docuSign link and mark the contract for accelerated review. I want procurement terms finalized by Aug 10 so legal can sign off before their internal deadline.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
